Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — we appreciated the performance numbers. Legal reviewed the draft Order Form and sent a few redlines focused on the SLA and support terms before we can route this internally for signature. Key asks are below:

• Uptime target: customer requests 99.9% uptime (instead of 99.95%) and explicit monthly measurement window.
• Service credits: proposal calls for 10% service credit of monthly fees for each full hour below the uptime target, capped at 50% per month.
• P1/P2 response times: 4-hour acknowledgement for P1, 24-hour for P2 (vs Redwood standard 1-hour / 4-hour).
• Maintenance windows: customer wants maintenance limited to a single 4-hour weekly window (weekend local) and 30 days' notice for planned maintenance >1 hour.
• Data / incident reporting: they want incident post-mortems within 5 business days.

Attached: Novacorp_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx with inline comments. From our side the procurement manager asked that we keep credits limited and keep faster response times, but they indicated flexibility if contract language is explicit. Can we get a legal-reviewed counter by end of week? If helpful, Tom (copied) will join a quick call.

Thanks,
Sophie

Team — forwarding Novacorp's redlines. Short ask: Legal + SalesOps, can we draft a realistic counter that protects Redwood's operational risk but keeps the commercial path clear? Points I think we should address up front: 

1) Uptime / measurement: propose keeping 99.95% as our default, but add an explicit measurement method based on monthly rolling window and exclude scheduled maintenance with prior notice.
2) Service credits: suggest a capped, tiered credit schedule (e.g., 10% for 99.7-99.95, 25% for 99.0-99.7, 50% for <99.0), with a monthly cap of one month's fees. This avoids per-hour credits that compound.
3) Response times: maintain 1-hour acknowledgement for P1 with target remediation window tied to root cause complexity; offer a 4-hour remediation SLA for critical cases as a commercial concession.
4) Maintenance: offer a weekly 4-hour maintenance window with optional second window for critical updates; Redwood to give 14 days' notice for planned maintenance >30 minutes and immediate notices for emergency maintenance.
5) Incident reports: propose post-mortem within 7 business days with an executive summary + remediation plan.

Lauren, can you draft specific clause language for uptime/credits and maintenance? Aditya, please confirm whether the remediation windows and tiered credit structure are operationally feasible. Evelyn, want to be sure this doesn't set a bad precedent for our mid-market procurements — any red flags commercially?

I put a tentative cadence: legal draft by Wed (6/3), internal review Thur (6/3-6/4), reply to customer Fri EOD or earlier.

Thanks — Rishi

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: SLA uptime & credits — Order Form #NOVA-127

All — reviewed Novacorp's redlines and drafted counter language. High-level legal position and proposed changes below (see attached redline PDF for exact markup):

• Uptime definition: We should keep 99.95% as the committed uptime. Measurement method: monthly rolling window, calculated as (total uptime minutes / total available minutes) in the month; exclude scheduled maintenance windows and customer-caused outages. This avoids cherry-picking short incidents.

• Service credits: we cannot accept uncapped per-hour credits. Proposed sliding scale in the Order Form:
  - >= 99.95%: no credit
  - 99.5% - 99.95%: 10% credit for the month
  - 99.0% - 99.5%: 25% credit for the month
  - < 99.0%: 50% credit for the month
Monthly cap: not to exceed 100% of the monthly recurring charge. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for downtime.

• Response times and escalation: keep 1-hour initial response for P1 incidents (acknowledgement and triage), target time-to-resolution to be commercially reasonable and dependent on root cause; offer a contractual target for P1 remediation of 8 hours as an exception (not a guaranteed fix), with a service credit trigger tied to availability rather than time-to-resolution.

• Maintenance windows: propose a primary weekly maintenance window of 02:00-06:00 UTC (covers most regions) and allow for scheduled maintenance with at least 14 days' notice for >1 hour changes. Emergency maintenance may be necessary; require we notify customer as soon as practicable and limit impact.

• Post-incident reporting: post-mortem within 7 business days with root cause analysis and remediation plan; limited exceptions for complex investigations.

Risks: Novacorp's 99.9% request + per-hour credits materially increases our exposure. The sliding-scale with a monthly cap mitigates unlimited exposure and aligns with market norms. If Sales insists on faster contractual remediation times, Legal will push for those to be SLA targets (commercial concessions) rather than hard liability triggers.

Attached: Redline_Respondent_Redwood_SLA_2026-06.pdf and suggested OrderForm_NOVA-127_2026-06.docx (clean). If everyone agrees, I'll incorporate these into a single Order Form and propose the DocuSign link.

Lauren

Hi Sophie / Tom / Novacorp Legal,

Thanks for the redlines and the clear asks — appreciate the transparency. We've reviewed with Legal and SalesOps and put together a balanced counter-proposal intended to address your concerns while managing operational risk on our side. Summary of agreed/asked changes below: 

1) Uptime: Redwood proposes 99.95% measured monthly on a rolling window, excluding scheduled maintenance and customer-caused events. We included precise measurement language in the attached Order Form.

2) Credits: rather than per-hour credits, we propose a sliding monthly credit scale (10% / 25% / 50%) with a monthly cap equal to one month's MRC and credits as the exclusive remedy for downtime. This prevents compounding credits for recurring short incidents.

3) Response & escalation: we will maintain 1-hour acknowledgement for P1. We can offer a commercial concession to include a 4-hour target for initial remediation steps for critical incidents (to be handled as a priority). Final remediation times are root-cause dependent, so we keep credits tied to availability.

4) Maintenance: primary weekly window proposed at 02:00-06:00 UTC; we will give at least 14 days' notice for planned maintenance >1 hour. For emergency maintenance we will notify as soon as practicable and minimize impact.

5) Post-incident reporting: Redwood will provide a post-mortem within 7 business days including root cause and remediation plan.

Attached are the clean Order Form and the redline for your review (OrderForm_NOVA-127_2026-06.docx; Redline_Respondent_Redwood_SLA_2026-06.pdf). If this aligns with your team's expectations, I'll upload the final Order Form to DocuSign and send the signing request (link below).
